issues.body:
At the same max-bounces setting Astroray allows 2 fewer glass bounces than Cycles. On the pkg325 thick-glass scene (white world; panes crossed by 2 / 4 / 6 glass interfaces, `benchmarks/showcase/spectral/pkg325`):

| interfaces k | Cycles 5.2 passes at cap | Astroray passes at cap |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | 3 |
| 4 | 3 | 5 |
| 6 | 5 | 7 |

So Cycles needs cap >= k-1, Astroray needs cap >= k+1. Same on CPU, GPU (OptiX build, software BVH agrees) and the addon route (`render(samples, settings.max_bounces, ...)`, no offset). Measured as ROI mean over a pure-sky ROI: dead (< 0.25 of 1.0) below the threshold, 0.89-1.0 at it. Evidence: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\astroray-evidence\2026-10-24\pkg325\s7` (`cyc_b*.npy`, `cpu_b*.npy`, `gpu_b*.npy`).

**Cycles (v5.2.0):** `intern/cycles/scene/integrator.cpp:222,226` hands the kernel `max_bounce + 1` and `max_transmission_bounce + 1`. `kernel/integrator/path_state.h:143-146` (total) and `:205-208` (transmission) set `PATH_RAY_TERMINATE_AFTER_TRANSPARENT` once the count reaches the limit; the NEXT surface then gets no BSDF (`surface_shader.h:1265-1268`, `shade_surface.h:497-499`). So the cap-th bounce scatters and one more surface is shaded.

**Astroray:** `include/raytracer.h:4012` loops `bounce < maxDepth` with maxDepth = the Blender value, so the continuation ray of vertex `maxDepth-1` is never traced (k interfaces need maxDepth >= k+1); the per-type limit at `:4883` (`typeCount >= typeLimit` -> break) takes the limit verbatim. GPU twin: `src/gpu/wavefront/stage_advance_device.cuh:2815` (`next_bounce >= max_depth`) and the `c_wfBounceLimit` block at `:2779` (`cnt >= lim`).

Effect: at equal settings Astroray renders strictly fewer bounces than Cycles (diffuse interreflection too, not only glass; not measured here). Found while building pkg325; not changed there (default `terminate` must stay as is until this is decided). Fix candidates: offset maxDepth / per-type limits by +1 like Cycles, on CPU and GPU together, then re-pin tests calibrated on the current counting.
issues.title: Bounce cap accounting: Astroray allows 2 fewer glass bounces than Cycles at the same cap (Cycles k-1 suffices for k interfaces, Astroray needs k+1)

Found by lane pkg326 (branch `lane/pkg326` 1c40c86c) while routing the Glass BSDF Thin Film sockets (#1136) into the native `principled` material.

At Roughness <= 0.03 the Principled sampler takes the delta-glass path with plain dielectric Fresnel on both backends (CPU `plugins/materials/principled.cpp` ~2013; GPU `kPrincipledDeltaGlassRoughness`), so a smooth glass or Principled surface ignores `Thin Film Thickness` / `Thin Film IOR` entirely. Cycles applies the thin-film Fresnel in the delta case too (`kernel/closure/bsdf_microfacet.h:795-917`, Blender v5.2.0). A soap bubble is smooth by construction, so this is the showcase case (pkg324 sp04) and the Glass node's default (Roughness 0).

Evidence: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\astroray-evidence\2026-10-24\pkg326\glass_bubble_montage.png` (rough Glass + film and Principled + film show interference glints; smooth Glass + film shows white glints); `tests/test_pkg326_glass_thin_film.py::test_smooth_glass_bubble_shows_film` is `xfail(strict)` on this; the addon reports smooth Glass with film per render until fixed.

Fix: apply the thin-film Fresnel (`thin_film_fresnel.h`, shared table) in the four delta-glass sites (CPU RGB/spectral, GPU RGB/spectral). The GPU shade kernel is register-saturated (REG 254): expect to route it through the existing closure parameters without new per-hit live state; measure with cuobjdump. Physics over look-parity (owner 2026-09-29): Cycles is right here, there is no reason to keep the delta path film-blind.
issues.title: Smooth glass (Roughness <= 0.03) ignores Thin Film on CPU and GPU: the Principled delta-glass path uses plain Fresnel; Cycles applies the film

Found by pkg324 (spectral showcase corpus, scene `sp09_classroom`, the Blender CC0 Classroom demo).

`blender_addon/__init__.py` (~L4048, the pkg274 missing-texture guard) checks `os.path.exists(bpy.path.abspath(bpy_image.filepath))`. For an image that is *linked from a library .blend* (`bpy_image.library` set, which is how the Classroom uses its `assets/*` group instances), the relative `//` path is relative to the LIBRARY file, not the main file, so `bpy.path.abspath(filepath)` without `library=` points at a non-existent folder. The texture is then replaced by the 1x1 magenta fallback and a DEGRADED entry is logged.

Evidence (Blender 5.2, `classroom.blend` with its `textures/` and `assets/` folders beside it): 32 file images are reported missing by `abspath(filepath)` and all 32 exist with `bpy.path.abspath(filepath, library=image.library)`. Astroray CPU at 480x270 / 48 spp renders every chair and desk metal/leather/wood part magenta and the blackboard white, while Cycles renders them textured; the render log lists `degraded base_leather.jpg: ...\classroom\..\..\textures\_baseTextures\base_leather.jpg` etc.

Fix sketch: resolve with `bpy.path.abspath(filepath, library=bpy_image.library)` (or `bpy_image.filepath_from_user()`) in the guard and in the loader that follows it; same for the other `bpy.path.abspath(...)` image/HDRI call sites (~L7167, L7471). Test: a two-file fixture (library .blend with an image + a main file linking it from a different folder) must render the texture, not magenta.

issues.body:
Found by pkg324 (spectral showcase corpus) while writing the analytic prism/dispersion checks.

`include/astroray/optical_presets.h` defines the `diamond` preset as `B = (0.3306, 4.3356, 0)`, `C = (0.0175, 0.1060, 0)`. These are Peter (1923) numbers, but Peter's formula uses the resonance WAVELENGTHS `lambda_1 = 0.175 um`, `lambda_2 = 0.106 um` in the denominator `l^2 - lambda_i^2`, while `sellmeierIOR` (plugins/materials/dielectric.cpp) and the GPU upload use the Schott form `l^2 - C_i` with `C_i` in um^2. The preset therefore has `C_1 = 0.0175` (should be `0.175^2 = 0.030625`) and `C_2 = 0.1060` (should be `0.106^2 = 0.011236`).

Evaluated with the engine's own formula:

| lambda (nm) | preset n | Peter 1923 n |
|---|---|---|
| 450 | 3.234 | 2.445 |
| 587.56 | 2.758 | 2.4175 |
| 650 | 2.671 | 2.411 |

so a `diamond` Sellmeier Glass renders with n_d = 2.76 and ~3x the real dispersion. (The preset's flat `ior` field is the correct 2.417, so only the dispersive path is wrong.)

Fix: `C = {0.030625f, 0.011236f, 0.0f}` for `diamond`, with a test that `iorAt(587.56) == 2.417 +- 0.002` on CPU and the GPU hero-wavelength path. `tests/test_pkg324_showcase_corpus.py::test_engine_diamond_preset_matches_peter1923` is a strict xfail pinned to this issue; remove the marker in the fix PR. The pkg324 diamond scene avoids the preset (manual Peter coefficients on the Sellmeier node), so the corpus is unaffected by the fix.
issues.title: diamond Sellmeier preset: n_d = 2.758 instead of 2.417 (C terms are not the squared resonance wavelengths)

issues.body:
Found by the cpp-abi-guard review of #1151 (#1125). Not an ABI issue; a planning/overflow follow-up.

`src/gpu/wavefront/gpu_wavefront_snapshot.cu` (`cuda_wavefront_render`): since #1125 the host pass plan uses the true transparent limit, `passDepth = max_depth + tLim + 1`, where it was capped at 31 before. Two consequences:

1. The 32-bit work-counter guard (`total_work + total_paths * (16 + passDepth + 2) > 0x7FFFFFFF` -> `throw std::runtime_error`) can now fire on large frames with alpha materials and a high `transparent_max_bounces`. Rough thresholds on the RTX 5070 Ti pool (pool = numPixels for frames above ~1.7M px): 1080p at 128 spp throws above tLim ~870; 4K throws above tLim ~210 (Blender's UI allows up to 1024). Before #1125 the same settings rendered silently with the pass count saturating at 31 (the bug #1125 fixed), so the new behaviour is honest but a failed render is worse UX than a capped one.
2. `wavefrontPoolSize` shrinks the pool from `work + pool * (16 + maxDepth + 2)` only; it does not know `passDepth`, so the pool is never shrunk for transparent passes before the guard throws.
3. `tLim + 1` is `int` arithmetic on a value settable from Python; near `INT_MAX` it overflows (UB). Clamp it.

Suggested fix: include `passDepth` in `wavefrontPoolSize`'s overflow check so the pool shrinks first; clamp the planning `tLim` to a sane bound (Blender max 1024) with `long long` arithmetic; if the counter still cannot fit, fall back to fewer in-flight paths rather than throwing. Keep the per-path `pass_count` lane as the true limit.
issues.title: Wavefront pass plan: high transparent_max_bounces on large frames can trip the 32-bit work-counter guard since #1125

issues.body:
From the i16 rough-glass Cycles-parity review (minor finding), deferred by lane i1120.

Cycles `bsdf_microfacet_sample` rejects a sampled direction on the wrong side of the **geometric** normal as well as the shading normal (Blender 5.2 `kernel/closure/bsdf_microfacet.h:854-862`, BSD-3-Clause):

```
if ((cos_NgO < 0) != do_refract || (cos_NO < 0) != do_refract) return LABEL_NONE;
```

Astroray's rough-glass sampler (CPU `principled.cpp` chooseAndSampleDir, GPU `gpu_pr_chooseAndSampleDir`) does only the shading-normal half. Neither `HitRecord` (`include/raytracer.h:368`) nor `GHitRecord` (`include/astroray/gpu_types.h:1001`) carries a geometric normal, so the Ng half cannot be added without new per-hit state. On the GPU that state sits in the register-saturated shade kernels (REG 254, lane rule 13), so it needs a design (e.g. a side table, or deriving Ng from the hit triangle on demand) and a cuobjdump REG/STACK + perf measurement.

Impact: smooth-shaded meshes only (shadow-terminator region, where N and Ng disagree); spheres and flat meshes have Ng == N. Cycles applies the same check to other closures, so a fix should cover them together.

Acceptance: a smooth-shaded low-poly glass mesh where reflection samples that go into the geometry (or refraction samples that leave it) are rejected on CPU and GPU, with a test that fails before; no REG/STACK regression on the principled shade kernels.
issues.title: Rough-glass (and microfacet) sampler lacks Cycles' geometric-normal side check (needs Ng in HitRecord/GHitRecord)

issues.body:
Found while attributing prod_curves_geometry `inner_backface` R 0.85 (#989 residual, lane for #1117).

**Not Backfacing.** Forcing the Mix factor to constant 1 leaves Cycles bit-identical on the ROI and Astroray equal within noise, so the back-face flag and the Pointiness chain are right. The residual survives a constant base colour (0.05, 0.4, 0.55) with specular 0.

**It is colour multi-bounce on a near-gamut-edge albedo.** Single bounce is exact (coplanar floor probe, uniform white world: Cycles/Astroray R 0.05 / 0.0497). Inside the bowl (>= 2 bounces), uniform white world, base (R, 0.4, 0.55), inner_backface R ratio: R=0.05 -> 0.117, 0.10 -> 0.656, 0.20 -> 0.925, 0.40 -> 1.013. Astroray R is exactly 0 on 50 % of the ROI pixels (Cycles min 0.011): the spectral product rho(lambda)^2 of a cyan reflectance has a negative red tristimulus, which the film clips; Cycles' RGB product 0.05^2 stays positive. Grey albedo matches (0.997). In the real scene: inner_backface R mean 0.853 (sd 0.029, 8 seeds, 64 spp), G/B 1.010.

Likely a documented spectral-vs-RGB divergence (physics over look-parity, owner 2026-09-29), not an engine bug; the question is whether to (a) declare `expected_divergence` for this ROI row in `gates_production.toml`, or (b) apply a gamut mapping for out-of-gamut spectral radiance at the film (affects all saturated multi-bounce scenes, both backends). The `phash <= 16` gate on reference-bank scene `sms-refractive-glass-sphere` (checked by `tests/test_pkg127_reference_gates_poly.py`) sits at the Monte Carlo noise floor. It passes only because `reference.png` is the same seed-17 noise realization the test renders, so any change to the sample stream fails it about half the time. This happened with pkg305 (#1003) and again with #1040.

Measured on CPU, 2026-10-03 (#1040 diagnosis):
- Two independent 4096-spp adaptive-off renders differ from each other by phash 14.
- Independent 1024-spp renders from the same engine differ pairwise by phash 12-22 (old and new adaptive engines alike).
- Old engine vs its own blessed reference at seeds 11/22/33: phash 18/24/16.
- Fixed engine vs an independent 4096-spp adaptive-off reference: phash 20/14/18/12 at seeds 17/11/22/33. SSIM, delta-E and bright_coverage pass with wide margins.

pHash bits are the 8x8 low-frequency DCT terms compared with their median. On this mostly dark, smooth image many terms sit near the median and flip with noise (camera->glass->light fireflies).

Fix direction (pick one, measure flip rates first): a seed-robust metric (e.g. pHash on a downsampled/blurred image, or exclude bits within a noise margin of the median), or a multi-seed reference with the gate judged over N seeds. Do not just raise the threshold.

#1040 re-blessed the reference at seed 17 on the fixed engine as a stopgap (same precedent as pkg305).

ROI means agree with the GPU and an independent oracle (arb_prism_sun beams 0.998-1.002), but the CPU traces ONE 3M-photon map per render() call while the GPU (#909) traces a fresh 4M map every 16 spp (<= 256 maps). Lead decision 2026-10-03: separate from the #959 PR.

Evidence: v2_dispersion_caustics CPU 256 spp vs GPU 1024 spp sheets in the #959 PR.

issues.body: Found by Terra review of lane au-coords (#1006). Object (#1006) and Generated (#847) coordinates are per-vertex attributes baked at the shutter-open pose; CPU `Triangle::interpolateAt` (include/astroray/shapes.h) and GPU `gpu_objectCoord` / `gpu_generatedCoord` (src/gpu/wavefront/stage_advance_device.cuh) recompute barycentrics from the hit point against the STATIC (shutter-open) vertices. For a motion-blurred object (add_triangles_bulk_motion) the hit at time t lies on the interpolated triangle, so the barycentrics and hence the pattern slide with the motion instead of staying attached (Cycles: object_inverse_position_transform with the motion-interpolated object transform, svm/tex_coord.h). Currently reported as an APPROXIMATED degradation by the addon for Object coordinates. issues.body:
Found in lane au-media (#961/#1019 fix, branch lane/au-media). After the light-tree segment pick fix, v2_media converges as 1/N (CPU N x relVar 34.9 / 33.1 / 30.5 at 16 / 64 / 256 spp; was 69 / 461 / 115), but the smoke_plume ROI still has N x relVar ~80-96 vs Cycles 1.2 (power sampler 31x, so not the light pick).

Cause (by reading, not yet ablated): the #925/#929 segment direct light draws its distance strategy from a lane mixture of truncated exponentials at the media hull's GLOBAL majorant (sum of per-medium maxDensity x extinction). For a sparse dense VDB (density 10) the samples pile up at the AABB entry or land in empty space, and the equiangular strategy about a far lamp is near-uniform over the hull, so the lit skin of the plume is rarely sampled. Cycles' distance strategy is the null-scattering tracked scatter collision with octree local majorants, MIS'd with equiangular via the null-scattering path pdf (Miller et al. 2019; kernel/integrator/shade_volume.h volume_direct_scatter_mis / volume_integrate_step_scattering, Apache-2.0). The pkg267 DDA majorant grid (include/astroray/volume/majorant_grid.h) exists but is not wired into tracking or the segment NEE.

Scope: CPU boundedSegmentDirect + GPU gpu_volumeSegmentDirect (kind 0); first an ablation (vb0, NEE-only, equiangular-only/distance-only) to confirm the owner, then a local-majorant (or tracked-collision) distance strategy with its exact pdf for MIS. Gate: smoke_plume per-sample relVar within 3x Cycles, means in band. Related: pkg306, #1019.
issues.title: Media: heterogeneous segment-NEE distance strategy uses the hull's global majorant (smoke VDB per-sample variance ~75x Cycles)

issues.body:
Follow-up from #1020 (fix branch lane/as-arb).

After #1020 the film converts XYZ to linear sRGB with the exact IEC 61966-2-1 matrix, then clips negative channels to 0 per channel (beauty and each light-path pass separately). Out-of-gamut colours (narrow-band lamps, dispersion caustics) therefore lose their negative channel: a sodium lamp renders B = 0 where Mitsuba writes -0.096 (pkg307 narrow-band wall).

Consequences:
- Sum-to-beauty for light-path passes holds exactly only when no pass has a negative channel: clipping is nonlinear, so sum(max(pass, 0)) != max(sum(pass), 0) in the clipped channel. Before #1020 the desaturation made it worse (mismatch in all channels). Codex Terra review of the #1020 fix.
- Per-pixel clipping of noisy out-of-gamut estimates biases those channels upward at low spp.

Decision needed: should beauty/passes keep negative scene-linear values (Cycles and Mitsuba write them to EXR), and where should clipping happen instead (display transform, PNG/8-bit outputs, denoiser input)? Touches every film site listed in include/astroray/spectral.h xyzToLinearSRGBExact callers plus downstream consumers (addon result passes, OIDN, tests that assume >= 0).
issues.title: Film: out-of-gamut channels clipped to 0 per pass/beauty; decide whether scene-linear output keeps negative values

issues.body:
Follow-ups left open by pkg299 Phase 0/1 (OptiX hardware traversal, default on for triangle-only scenes):

1. **Time to first sample.** The GPU path still runs the CPU BVH build and the host flatten/upload (`buildAcceleration()` + `buildSceneArrays`) before the OptiX accel build. The spec's criterion is that the heavy scene's first call drops by at least 1.5 s. The software BVH also still backs the photon pre-pass, ReSTIR, SMS and the transparent-shadow walk, so each of those needs an OptiX route or an explicit fallback first.
2. **Refit on transform-only edits.** A pkg114 transform edit invalidates the scene cache, so every GAS and the IAS are rebuilt (62 ms per render on the 2M-triangle Cornell). This should refit or rebuild only the IAS and keep the GAS.
3. **Shared OptiX context with the denoiser.** Traversal (`src/gpu/optix/optix_pipeline.cpp`) and the pkg70 denoiser each create their own `OptixDeviceContext` on the same CUDA primary context, with separate function tables via `OPTIX_ENABLE_SDK_MIXING`.
4. **Transparent-shadow walk.** Scenes with Principled alpha < 1 (`HasAlphaShadow`) still trace shadow rays on the software BVH, while closest hits use OptiX. The walk could move into `__raygen__shadow` (closest-hit loop plus a material alpha lookup).

Phase 2 (spheres, curves, motion) is tracked in the pkg299 spec itself.

Found by the pkg310 production corpus (burn-down: `.astroray_plan/docs/pkg310-production-corpus-burndown.md`).

**Root cause.** The op-VM has no per-hit shading inputs. Layer Weight (Facing/Fresnel), Fresnel, and Geometry (Backfacing, Pointiness) reach the compiler as "unsupported node type in op-VM chain: LAYER_WEIGHT / FRESNEL / NEW_GEOMETRY" and the whole chain is flattened to grey (reported: `approximated op-VM: shader chain on 'Base Color' not representable ... flattened to grey`). They need per-hit data (incident direction vs normal, front/back flag, curvature) that the hit record does not carry to the program.

**Evidence** (Astroray / Cycles ROI-mean ratio, seed 278):
- `prod_car_paint` (Layer Weight Facing -> Mix base/flake tint, Fresnel -> Metallic): `lit_front` G = 4.64 CPU / 4.60 GPU, `limb_grazing` L = 1.50.
- `prod_curves_geometry` (Backfacing + Pointiness -> Mix): `inner_backface` R = 4.65 CPU / 4.58 GPU, `outer_front` R = 0.36.

**Category:** per-hit input. **Backends:** CPU and GPU (identical export gap).
**Materials unblocked:** prod_car_paint, prod_curves_geometry (the latter also needs the Curves issue).
**Observable:** `prod_car_paint` `lit_front` G within 1 +- 0.05 on CPU and GPU (now 4.64); `prod_curves_geometry` `inner_backface` R within 1 +- 0.06 (now 4.65).

The pkg284 corpus v2 bands (`gates_v2.toml`, `mc_tolerance.py`) take the Astroray CPU sigma from seeds 278-282. The CPU tile loop seeds its white-noise stream as `mt19937(seed + tileIndex)`, so seed s+1 replays seed s shifted by one tile. The five renders are correlated and the per-ROI CPU sigma is underestimated.

Measured (CPU, 64 spp, main 775a5d6b, `astra_run/AP/ap-305/renders`), relative sigma of the ROI mean:

| ROI | seeds 278-282 (= toml `cpu_sigma`) | 15 independent seeds (278 + 10000 k) |
|---|---|---|
| v2_camera_geometry mesh_volume g | 0.0068 | 0.0105 |
| v2_camera_geometry mesh_volume L | 0.0072 | 0.0107 |
| v2_dispersion_caustics beam_through_prism L | 0.0156 | 0.0257 |

Effect: single-seed (278) rows whose Astroray mean sits a little off Cycles fail whenever the random stream changes. pkg305 (stratified camera group) changes it: `mesh_volume` g/b/L (0.974 vs tol 0.022) and `beam_through_prism` L (0.941 vs pin tol 0.0585) fail at seed 278, although their 15-seed means equal the baseline (mesh_volume L 0.9855 vs 0.9849; beam new/base 0.996).

Fix: re-derive the bands with independent seeds (e.g. `--seeds 278 10278 20278 30278 40278`) for the Cycles, CPU and GPU legs, then remove the provisional rows that cite this issue.
issues.title: Corpus v2 bands: CPU sigma from correlated seeds 278-282 is underestimated (mt19937 seed+tile streams overlap)

In the pkg294 media cubes, Astroray's per-sample variance is near Cycles' (1.13x / 0.74x / 0.45x) but at 64 spp it is 5.23x / 2.24x / 1.14x, because Cycles' variance x spp drops 0.495 -> 0.109 from 1 to 64 spp (Sobol-Burley/PMJ QMC) while Astroray's stays flat (0.56 -> 0.57). Likely also a large part of #763 (corpus scenes noisier than Cycles at equal spp). Relates to the #858 decision to flip the pkg224 progressive sampler on by default (owner 2026-09-29).

Scope: a QMC sampler (Cycles Sobol-Burley, Apache-2.0; cite-algorithm) with per-dimension decorrelation on CPU and GPU, means unchanged in MC band, variance x spp falling on the pkg294 cubes and corpus v2.

Checklist for judging whether the off-thread viewport worker should become the default. Runs in your own Blender; no isolated instance needed.

1. Open `blender_addon/scenes/metal_sweep.blend`, engine Astroray, device GPU, 3D view in Rendered shading.
2. Baseline (worker OFF, today's default): orbit with MMB for ~5 s, then let it settle.
3. Turn the worker on without restarting: Python console, `import os; os.environ['ASTRORAY_VIEWPORT_WORKER']='1'`, then toggle the view out of Rendered and back.
4. Repeat the orbit. Watch: does the image update while you drag, or only after you release?
5. Release and wait ~3 s: the preview should sharpen to full resolution, not stay blocky.
6. While a render is refining, drag a panel slider and open a menu. The UI should stay responsive.
7. Material storm: drag Base Color back and forth for ~5 s. The colour should track the slider, with no stale frames.
8. Emission: set Principled Emission Strength 0 -> 5. The object should glow and light its surroundings (needs PR #843).
9. Move an object with G, and change a light's Power. Both should show immediately.
10. Repeat steps 4-9 on a heavy scene of your own (roughly 100k+ triangles).
11. Note anything that looks frozen, stale, blocky after settling, or noisier than before.
12. Known gaps: orbit on light scenes is slower with the worker ON (#854); the storm row is still commit-bound (#855); orbit preview colour noise (#856); the worker ignores the camera render border (#857).

Verdict to record: is the worker better than the synchronous path for you on both scenes, and is anything in step 11 a blocker for making it the default?

issues.body:
## Context

pkg265 (PR #778) implements the Heitz 2016 multiple-scattering microfacet dielectric random walk for rough glass, replacing the single-scatter + pkg264 #771 dead-sample delta reroute. The walk uses a **plain-dielectric** Fresnel/transmission coefficient in its phase function.

The second cycles-parity review (CRITICAL #2) found that a **thin-film** rough Principled glass (thin_film_thickness > cutoff, roughness > kDeltaGlassRoughness) was being routed through this plain-dielectric walk. The walk:
- sets `isDelta=true` (skip-NEE contract) but `eval()`/`pdf()` still return the nonzero thin-film single-scatter f for a thin-film glass â†’ **direct light double-counted** (NEE + full-weight emitter hit) up to ~2x on the directly-lit part;
- carries plain-dielectric Fresnel throughput â†’ **drops the iridescence colour** on the sampled path.

## Fix landed in #778

Thin-film rough glass is gated OUT of the walk (`filmActive()` branch in `principled.cpp` `chooseAndSampleDir` + `transmissionPdf`): it falls back to the origin/main single-scatter rough-transmission sampler (incl. the pkg264 #771 reroute), so sample == eval == pdf are all single-scatter thin-film, no double count, iridescence preserved on the eval path. Disney glass has no thin-film path, so no change there.

## This follow-up

Make the multiple-scattering walk **thin-film-aware**: replace the plain-dielectric Fresnel/transmission coefficient in the Heitz dielectric phase function (`include/astroray/microsurface_dielectric.h`) with the thin-film iridescence Fresnel/transmittance (the `thin_film_fresnel.h` coefficients already used by `transmissionEvalRGB`/`transmissionEvalSpectral`), so thin-film rough glass gets the physically-correct multiple-scattering treatment AND its iridescence colour on every bounce of the walk. Then the `filmActive()` single-scatter fallback in `principled.cpp` can be removed.

Non-trivial: the walk crosses the interface many times with alternating entering/exiting film-IOR adjustment; the per-bounce thin-film transmittance must telescope correctly (cf. the etaÂ² telescoping validated in `test_pkg265_walk_eta.cpp`).

Priority: P2 (the #778 fix is correct and unbiased; this is a quality/parity improvement for the thin-film-glass corner).
issues.title: Thin-film-aware multiple-scattering microfacet glass walk (pkg265 follow-up)

issues.body:
## Summary

Capture a longer-horizon architectural direction surfaced by the Blender-integration parity research (2026-05-30): **expose the Astroray engine core as an engine-agnostic renderer** â€” usable standalone (its own scene-description entry point) and, eventually, as a **USD / Hydra render delegate** â€” with the Blender addon as a thin integration shim over it.

This is a **future / milestone-evaluation** item. It is intentionally **not scheduled** and has no package yet. Filed so it is not lost.

## Why (research finding)

Cycles is built both as a standalone application (its own XML scene/shader API) and as a **Hydra render delegate**, letting it run inside usdview / Houdini Solaris / Omniverse entirely outside Blender. Its Blender addon is just an integration layer over an engine-agnostic core.

- Cycles repo README: *"Cycles can be built as a standalone application or a Hydra render delegate."* (https://github.com/blender/cycles)
- Cycles standalone dev docs: https://developer.blender.org/docs/features/cycles/standalone/

**This validates Astroray's existing shape** (C++/CUDA core + thin Python/Blender addon). The action item is to keep that boundary clean and, as a forcing function, consider a standalone scene-description entry point â€” with a USD/Hydra delegate as the long-term payoff.

## Why it matters

- **Reach:** Astroray usable in Houdini/Omniverse/usdview, not just Blender.
- **Architecture hygiene:** a standalone entry point keeps the engine from accreting Blender-API assumptions.
- **Journal/paper story:** "engine-agnostic GR-capable renderer with a Hydra delegate" is a strong contribution framing.

## Scope sketch (not committed)

- [ ] Audit/strengthen the engine-core â†” Blender-addon boundary (no `bpy` assumptions in core).
- [ ] Standalone scene-description entry point (JSON/USD-lite) exercising the engine without Blender.
- [ ] (Long term) Hydra render delegate (`HdRenderDelegate`) prototype â€” note Cycles labels its own Hydra delegate experimental.

## References

- Blender-integration parity report: `.astroray_plan/docs/blender-integration-parity-report-2026-05-30.md` (cross-cutting recommendation #3).
- Cycles standalone + Hydra delegate (above).

_Filed from owner request (rabbit-hole #2), 2026-05-30._
